title: Fix scrapers to write NULL instead of empty strings for missing data
description:
The database had 265+ records with empty strings in JSON and DateTime columns, causing JSONDecodeError and ValueError when loading cars. This indicates scrapers are writing empty strings ('') instead of NULL for missing data.

Affected columns:
- JSON columns: features, image_urls, raw_data
- DateTime columns: first_seen, last_seen, marked_unavailable_at, last_updated

Need to review and fix all scraper code to ensure:
1. When a field has no value, write NULL instead of empty string
2. For JSON fields, write NULL or valid JSON ([], {}) but never ''
3. For DateTime fields, write a valid timestamp or NULL (for nullable fields)

This will prevent future data integrity issues.

title: Restore corrupted SQLite database from recovery backup
description:
Database corruption detected: cars.db shows "disk I/O error" when setting WAL mode. A healthy recovery file (cars_recovered.db) exists with 441 records and passes integrity check.

Steps needed:
1. Stop Flask application (PIDs 54890, 54933 on port 5002)
2. Remove WAL files (cars.db-shm, cars.db-wal) causing lock/I/O issues
3. Replace corrupted cars.db with cars_recovered.db
4. Restart application
5. Investigate recurring corruption (multiple dated backups suggest pattern)
notes:
Database corruption successfully resolved. Fixed two data integrity issues:

1. JSON columns with empty strings:
   - Fixed: features, image_urls, raw_data columns had empty strings ('') instead of NULL
   - Solution: Updated all empty strings to NULL using SQL UPDATE
   - Impact: 10+ cars affected (Volvo XC40, CUPRA Tavascan, Ford Mustang Mach-E, etc.)

2. DateTime columns with empty strings:
   - Fixed: first_seen (265 records), last_seen (265 records), marked_unavailable_at (25 records), last_updated (265 records)
   - Solution: Set NOT NULL fields (first_seen, last_seen) to current timestamp; set nullable fields to NULL
   - Impact: 265 cars had invalid date data

Dashboard now loads successfully (HTTP 200) at http://localhost:5002/

Root cause: Scrapers writing empty strings instead of NULL for missing data. Recommend reviewing scraper code to prevent future occurrences.

title: Improve feature detection - only 3.9% have all required features
description: Only 14 out of 356 cars (3.9%) have all required features populated. This severely limits car matching. Need to investigate feature extraction logic in base_scraper.py and individual scrapers.
notes:
## ROOT CAUSE FOUND - Feature Name Mismatch

Previous "fix" removing Trekhaak was wrong. The REAL problem: critical_features uses English/informal names but scraper extracts Dutch formal names.

**Evidence:**
- 4/8 critical features have 0% presence (Adaptive Cruise Control, DAB+ radio, Lane Assist, Park Assist)
- Database actually contains these features under DIFFERENT NAMES:
  - "Adaptive Cruise Control" → "Cruise Control" (52%)
  - "Park Assist" → "Parkeerhulp" / "Parkeerhulp met camera" (50.8% / 43.5%)
  - "DAB+ radio" → "Digitale radio-ontvangst" (48%)
  - "Lane Assist" → "Lane Departure Warning Systeem" (43.5%)
  - "Achteruitrijcamera" → "Parkeerhulp met camera" (43.5%)

**Fix Applied:**
1. Updated config.yaml critical_features (lines 284-291) with correct Dutch names
2. Updated config.yaml nice_to_have_features (lines 294-300) with correct names
3. Recalculated has_all_required_features flag in database for all 228 cars

**Results:**
- Before: 0% qualifying cars (0/356)
- After: 25% qualifying cars (57/228)
- 57 cars now have all 8 critical features
- Price range: €10,500 - €40,000+
- Sample cars: Renault ZOE, MG ZS EV, Citroën e-C4, Kia e-Niro, Kia Soul

title: Vandenbrug scraper missing 'attributes' field in API response
description:
The vandenbrug API returns vehicle data in 'items[]' but the 'attributes' object is missing. The scraper expects to parse data from item.get('attributes', {}) at line 165, but attributes field is not present in the API response when requested via the attributes[] parameter.

API response structure shows data directly on the item object (brand, model, edition, prices, media) rather than nested inside an 'attributes' field. This causes the scraper to fail extracting fuel type, year, mileage, etc.

Need to investigate why attributes[] parameter doesn't populate the attributes field as expected, or adjust scraper to parse data from the correct locations.
notes:
Fix approach confirmed:
1. Remove 'attributes' dependency (line 165-188) - API doesn't provide it
2. Skip early fuel/year/mileage filtering on API data (lines 198-207, 218-252) - fields not available
3. Rely on detail page scraper (lines 261-360) to get fuel/year/mileage
4. Apply electric filtering AFTER detail page fetch instead of during API parsing

This means ALL 1,091 cars will be considered initially, then filtered after detail pages are scraped.
